risks.name: Cardiovascular adaptations
risks.summary: Fluid shift and reduced load cause cardiovascular deconditioning and remodeling that can impair performance in flight and after landing.

risks.name: Bone fracture due to spaceflight-induced bone changes
risks.summary: Weight-bearing bones lose density without countermeasure exercise, so a fracture may occur after flight during activities that were safe before.

risks.name: Reduced cardiorespiratory and musculoskeletal fitness
risks.summary: Reduced gravity lowers aerobic capacity and muscle strength, power and endurance, which can impair mission tasks and health.

risks.name: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
risks.summary: Eye and brain structural changes develop in flight and can lead to short- or long-term vision changes.

risks.name: Adverse cognitive or behavioral conditions
risks.summary: Long isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, radiation and altered gravity can lead to adverse cognitive or behavioral changes and psychiatric disorders.

risks.name: Sleep loss, circadian desynchronization and work overload
risks.summary: Crews sleep about 6 h per night in flight; sleep loss, shifted schedules and workload reduce performance and health.

risks.name: Altered immune response
risks.summary: Spaceflight causes persistent immune dysregulation, reactivation of latent herpesviruses, rashes and hypersensitivity reactions.

risks.name: Inadequate food and nutrition
risks.summary: Limited ability to supply adequate food on long missions can cause performance decrements, illness and long-term health effects.

risks.name: Radiation carcinogenesis
risks.summary: Galactic cosmic rays and solar particle events raise the lifetime risk of cancer; NASA limits career dose to 600 mSv.
